title: Homonyms and the Uncreated Nature
english: Of Christ, the spirit of truth, as John announces from the Savior: 'If you love me, you have kept my commandments; and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, so that the spirit of truth may be with you forever' (John 14:15-17). And again in his first epistle: 'And the spirit is the one testifying that the spirit is the truth' (1 John 5:6), which is similar to saying of the Son: 'I am the truth' (John 14:6).

A divine spirit and the breath of the Pantokrator and a lover of mankind, according to the phrase of Job and according to Moses mentioned a few verses earlier in this chapter. The Holy Spirit was praised and [is] light, in whom also we are enlightened, just as the apostle writes: 'that he might give you a spirit of wisdom and of revelation, in the knowledge of him, having the eyes of your heart enlightened' (Ephesians 1:17-18), and as David sings: 'for with you is the fountain of life; in your light we shall see light' (Psalm 36:9); that is to say, in your Son, the radiance of your glory, your Holy Spirit. And: 'The light of your face has been shown to us, Lord' (Psalm 89:15). For what else would the Spirit be, if he proceeds from the Father or out of the Light? Concerning which John sang in the first epistle: 'God is light' (1 John 1:5), and in the Gospel concerning the Only-begotten: 'was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world' (John 1:9), and: 'I am the light, I am the life' (John 11:25).

It is nothing wonderful, then, if being one and always having [the same nature], he is glorified with differing designations. For his divinity, being ungraspable by the words of mortals, they praise with differing [designations] and with names, according to the power of the energies which come to us. As for those representing the doctrine of Macedonius, becoming more of their heresy than of the truth, nothing is happening to those looking at the logical arguments. For they are mythologically seizing upon words, as if one should not pay attention to homonyms, or synonyms, or similar expressions.

For the 'good' name of God, he says, is entwined with 'one God,' but regarding the Holy Spirit, the 'good' name is not joined with 'one God.' And again: good, he says, was written to be even a man, as he says: 'do good, Lord, to the good' (Luke 6:35), and: 'the good man brings good things out of the good treasure' (Luke 6:45). Similarly, he says, good [is] the...

Evenly and without soul, as when one prophesies: 'If you will and listen to me, eat the good things of the earth' (Ps 34:8). But also regarding unstable things it is said: 'It is good to confess to the Lord' (Ps 51:15). Similarly, it is said a man is called holy, and a power of God, and a worm, where it is written: 'My strength, my great power' (Isa 48:16), and the Savior says: 'The powers of the heavens shall be shaken' (Matt 24:29).

And this I say: that the argument regarding homonyms and similar words applies to heterousious things, but not to the Holy Spirit and Him whose Spirit He is, and moreover to the Son. For the Scripture adds to the homonyms or synonyms a safeguard from itself, by enclosing the syllable 'my' or 'your' or the word 'holy' or 'good'; that is, either as from God it says: 'my spirit,' or as from David and us: 'your good spirit shall guide me' (Ps 23:6).

Therefore, it is necessary to be persuaded by those scriptural testimonies which are much more effective, and to know that the Holy Spirit has homonymy or synonymy and similar words toward God and His only-begotten Son, having mentioned those with similar names, not toward creatures because there is found sometimes a homonymy in them.

For even if we should give a name or a word to participate in God, it is not in essence or in the energy of power and sanctification. For these things do not exist at all by nature; but by comparison to the evil, the good and the sin, that is, the passion, the holy has been arranged; for the not very evil and sinful, that is, the passible, the good and holy is spoken of here.

For just as wickedness and sin, that is, passion and weakness, are not found in the one Holy Spirit, being ungenerated; so also in none of the generated things is the good and holy and powerful according to perfection, but according to participation; and where these are not anywhere according to perfection, nowhere is the ungenerated. For where there is darkness, nowhere is the light; and 'where there is night, not day.' And it is said also to Hermes Trismegistus: 'It is impossible for the good to be in generation, but only in the ungenerated. Just as participation is given to all in matter, so also to the good.' Therefore, the Holy Spirit is similar and equal to the Father and...

title: The Distinction of the Holy Spirit from Angels
english: Of the only-begotten deity: and from such a judgment it is shown that he himself exists by nature as holiness and goodness and power, being one out of the one. Since against their contention, neither the most good and merciful in nature shall the Son still be good; because 'one God' does not have a unified nature. Nor indeed shall the most philanthropic and entirely merciful Father and the Son possess the aforementioned names of deity; but rather through them they shall be demoted, as it is the custom to speak to heretics, to us who are homonymous. Be merciful, O Holy Trinity.

But the Son, he says, having been co-begotten, possesses goodness by nature, and all the other things that the Father has. But also the Holy Spirit, having proceeded together, is good by nature, and all the things the God Father has.

3.30 If, therefore, their discussion was about accidental or worldly matters, it would have been well for them to have need to weave certain myths, and with an Aristotelian-seeming skill and a technique in words, like Eunomius, to twist the matter and to overshadow the truth; 3.31 but now Paul teaches: 'unless you believe, you will not understand at all' (Luke 24:25), and: 'the wisdom of men is foolishness with God' (1 Cor 3:19). And the words concerning the glorious Spirit ought not to be made more wise than human reasoning. For reproach does not harm the Holy Spirit, nor furthermore from hearing do the insults and the mockeries of the heretics come, to whom the evil thought has fallen upon; but those using such things will suffer endlessly and will act similarly to those attempting to mock this light, which has its strength from the unapproachable light, and defile it with their words. 3.32 And it is necessary to believe that the teaching from the saints is able to impart more glory than that from men.

It is therefore fitting for us to take care not, through an excessive goodwill, to draw down the divine which is upon them into the results of creatures by sophistries regarding their own heresy, and through these to give birth to a love of destruction to the simpler and more ignorant, and to lead forward into a desire for greater sins.
4. Regarding those heretical ones saying: God is spirit; and how the Holy Spirit is spirit of the spirit? And again: the angels, therefore, they say, are not...

Are they from God and holy and spirits of God? But while they are being sent out, they are simple, direct, and perfect, yet they corrupt the choice of sacred words through ignorance, by which the Father God willed His Spirit to be arranged with Him, as the only-begotten Word, and His being removed from creation and exceeding [all] is secured, wherefore also He is thrice-sung, they say; how is the Spirit, the Holy Spirit, a Spirit?

For although this is written and shown; but the 'how' exceeds the knowledge of mind and word of us, and even of angels. For just as the God-Word was begotten from Him as a Father exists, so from Him and with Him the Holy Spirit was manifested; and in this especially His ungraspability is shown, in that what is appearing and being is impossible to be by Him through creation. For what is the difference between the uncaused and life-giving nature and the created and being-made-life-giving? Nor is it possible for the Spirit not to be consubstantial and equal to that from whom he is. Therefore he is also holy by nature.

The angels, he says, are they not from God and holy and spirits of God? They are from God, in that they have become under His command, as all things; but holy after being sanctified, like men; and spirits, insofar as they are incorporeal to us.

They are not called spirits of God or from God or proceeding from the Father or divine or spirits of truth or spirits of holiness; but ministering angels and heavenly bodies because they infinitely distance and subtilize themselves from the uncreated Spirit of God, according to the writer who is an experienced apostle: 'bodies on earth and bodies in heaven' (Col 1:2).

For just as the spirits of the winds are not according to them, neither are they according to the Holy Spirit of God. For they were created, but they did not proceed from the substance of God and Father; they do not regenerate us, they do not make us gods, they do not forgive sins, they do not give life, they do not create, they do not sanctify, they do not judge, but they also are judged. For 'you,' he says, 'shall also judge angels' (1 Cor 6:3).
Nor are the powers in them of the heavens. They are not in places, undefinable and immeasurable in intervals. For Gabriel speaking to Daniel, or announcing the Theotokos...

title: The Unvarying Illumination of Wisdom and the Nature of the Spirit
english: by essence, as by thought

And to him in Spain, and in another place, having been granted by him a wisdom that is simple and without wavering until the end of the earth, he imparts it; not in one way now, only to suddenly appear in another, nor more to one and less to another, breathing upon them, but always shining similarly to each one both together and distinctly, just as the one who said: 'I am with you all the days until the completion of the age' (Matt 28:20).

Since they transfer to God and Father the theology lying with John where it is said: 'God is Spirit' (1 John 4:16), saying because it is written that he is Spirit, and also because it is written: 'The Spirit of our face is Christ Lord' (2 Cor 3:3);—will they then also count the Father and the Son as Spirit among the other functional spirits? If it is not so, then the Holy Spirit is not understood among the other spirits, for he is not an archangel. For Michael and Gabriel and those like them are archangels; and with them, even heretics would not say that the Holy Spirit of God is ranked. Wherefore then, do they examine where he is to be ranked, or among which creatures? For after God, we were not taught from the Scriptures another rational nature, nor of the many spirits and of bodies like us.

Still, they lead [us] sophistically from what is set forth: that the Father and the Son are 'true,' but the Spirit is written as 'truth,' as if this were different. But it is the same, as it has been shown by the first argument, and this does not differ from that.

Concerning those saying, 'Since the only-begotten is the Word of God, what shall we call the Spirit?' and concerning the testimony that the Son is only-begotten. The Holy Spirit is one and only; and again the Son is the Word; the Holy Spirit, the Word. And concerning comparison; and concerning the fact that there is no paradigm of the incomparable essence.

Toward these things, the most varied and manifold according to the word—I do not know, if not even according to opinion—but certainly that even this, the heretics of the stranger [to us] of the simpler and truer teaching, frequently turning over the same words, say: 'The God Word was called only-begotten, because the Holy Spirit is not from the subsistence of the Father.
